newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel rises against dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel rises against dollar, basket.

text.p: The shekel gained on Tuesday against the dollar and the basket of key foreign currencies following the Bank of Israel's decision to leave interest rates unchanged, dealers said.
The central bank announced on Monday, after the setting of the representative rate, that its key lending rate would stay at an annualised 15.2 percent in December.

"The shekel started rising (on Monday) against the dollar immediately after the rate announcement, despite the dollar's rise against the mark. On Tuesday this trend continued but the rise was very moderate," said a dealer at Israel Discount Bank.
"During the day the shekel moved in a narrow range and activity was low. The main activity was inter-bank trading," the dealer said.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2420 shekels against 3.2470 on Monday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, closed at 3.6376 shekels against 3.6551 on Monday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8770 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8889 on Monday and against the mark at 2.1232 shekels against 2.1450 on Monday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.2380 shekels.
